Text.Text: Force-Bonded Beast. The thread is whole in you now, both directions, always. Nothing left in that den can teach either of you anything new. Go. Mind the thread; it minds you back.
Not you, first. It. I feel the thread between you, thin still, more suggestion than cord. Go. Let it thicken before you bring it here again.

There. I see it now, faint but real, a thread trying to grow between you and yours. The Grotto Apex Den is full of wyverns whose threads were cut. The handlers who held that den forced bonds on them, then severed them when the beasts turned. The handlers are gone. The wyverns remain, and they tear at any thread that comes near. Go to the den on Dathomir. End six of the Young Wyverns, the ones roosting nearest the way in. Any Young Wyvern will do, every wyvern in that den was cut the same way. But the thread has to be doing its work: a kill counts while your beast's Warding Howl is shielding you, or when your beast's Force Touch lands on the wyvern. Bring me the Force-Bonded Beast Grotto Track Slate from their roost; it once mapped where a proper rite could be spoken.

Take the key; it is yours now, as much as the gate is. South out of these ruins to the Tarnished Jungles North, north into the Desert, west past the Tribe Village into the Grottos, then north-east along the canyon to the Grottos' east entrance. It opens on the south end of the Grotto Caverns; the den waits a short walk north-west, on the west side by the water, a moss-topped rock mound with a dark cave mouth. Go slow at the threshold, both of you. The den answers to patience before it answers to force.

A true bond is spoken, not forced. Thread laid between two willing lives, tightened by trust instead of chain. The handlers found the old rite and cut the willing part out of it entirely. What was left, they forced onto every wyvern in the den. It is not binding. It is leashing with extra words.

In the old rite, the slate marked where the ground itself remembered a bond made honestly, a place returned to, generation after generation. The handlers used it to find beasts still uncorrupted, so they could corrupt them first. The Young Wyverns roost on it now. Bring it back and the ground remembers correctly again.

Because their own threads were forced on them, then cut. A beast that has only known a forced bond learns that every thread is a chain, so they tear at any they find, yours included. That is the handlers' doctrine, still alive in their beasts: control the ending, since you cannot control the truth of the beginning.
Six Young Wyverns still tearing at what should be tied. Let the Warding Howl shield you or the Force Touch land. The slate waits in their roost.
The thread between you is thicker already. Show me what you carried out.
The ground remembers again. That is no small thing. Rest, both of you. There is a second knot to tie, when you are ready.

The Goad-Scarred Wyverns, the older ones deeper in, still carry forced bonds, with no one left on the other end of them. They have learned to mistake pain for devotion. That is not a knot. That is a wound wearing a knot's shape. Go back to the Grotto Apex Den. End five of them, with the Warding Howl shielding you or your beast's Force Touch upon each; any Goad-Scarred Wyvern counts. Bring me the Force-Bonded Beast Resonant Fang Charm one of them still wears.
Same gate, deeper trail. Walk it together this time, truly together. Let it lead, or you lead. Either is honest. Just do not drag.

The fang charm once marked a bond strong enough to hum on its own, no rite needed to prove it. The handlers hung it on a wyvern to borrow a hum they never earned. Take it back and the hum means something again.

Force a bond, and somewhere under the obedience the beast is still choosing, every single day, not to break your neck. That choice does not vanish. It waits. A forced bond is a debt that always comes due, usually at the worst possible moment for whoever forced it.

The handlers starved them of the choice entirely, goad and reward until there was no space left to choose anything else. It looks like loyalty. It is closer to drowning slowly enough that the beast forgets water ever felt different.
Five Goad-Scarred Wyverns, five wounds wearing knots. Bring the charm back true.
The hum is on you both now. Let me hear it properly.
True again. Second knot, tied honest. You are further along this rite than either of you know yet.

Handler's Wraid holds the deeper weave, a wraid the handlers bound before any of the wyverns. Every forced thread in that den was tied through him, and his own bond has been forced so long it no longer looks like one. No single thread can unpick a weave that size. Bring two others, with their own honest bonds if they carry them, and cut his weave apart together. End him. Bring me the Force-Bonded Beast Cracked Apex Totem bound to his harness.
Go to the gate together, all your threads at once. He will feel more than one coming. Let him. That is the point.
Forced so long the beast inside it has forgotten it was ever asked. I do not know if there is anything left in there to save. That is not pity talking. It is the truest answer I have.

The cracked apex totem once marked the den's oldest honest bond, the first thread the rite was ever spoken over. The handlers cracked it and bound it to him, to say the first bond was theirs now. Bring it back whole and the first bond is honored again, even after everything.

One thread pulls at a weave and the weave simply moves around it, absorbs it, keeps pulling from every other direction instead. Three threads pulling together do not move around each other. They cut. That is not strategy. That is just what a weave cannot survive.
Handler's Wraid still wears a weave instead of a thread. Bring your own bonds when you go.
All your threads, still whole, still tied. Let me see what came off him.
The first bond, honored again. That is a rite older than this den's corruption, spoken true for the first time in longer than I want to guess. The Den Elder Wyverns will have felt that.

Four remain in the deepest part of the den, the Den Elder Wyverns: the eldest wyverns, the first of their kind the handlers ever forced. Their threads were braided into one cord, and a cord does not fray one strand at a time; it holds until every strand is cut at once. Bring your bonds back in, all of you together. End the four, with the Warding Howl shielding you or your beast's Force Touch upon each; any Den Elder Wyvern counts. Bring me the Force-Bonded Beast Den-Mother's Fang Token from their roost.
Go as one weave yourselves, then, if you are going to unmake theirs. Four strands, cut together, or not cut at all.

Every corruption I have named to you. Force. Leash. Goad. Sever what turns on you first. The handlers braided it into those four as if it were the original rite, and every wyvern hatched since learned it from them. A lie is strongest when no one left alive remembers the true words.

The den-mother's own bond, older than any of us. The handlers left her token in that roost so no keeper of the true rite could ever claim it. Whole again, it is proof the true rite still exists underneath everything they built on top of it.

The rite, spoken honestly, over every beast still capable of choosing. Not leashed. Not goaded. Asked, the way it was always meant to be asked. I have waited a long time to speak it properly again. You are the reason I finally will.
Four strands still holding their false cord. Go cut it, together.
Every bond among you still whole. Show me the token.

Whole, and warm with the truth again. One thread left down there, and it is the one every other thread was copied from, badly. You are close enough now that I will speak plainly: you are ready for the last knot.

The last thread is his. Old Wraid is the eldest wraid, the first beast the handlers ever forced the rite upon. His bond was forced past anything the others suffered, until it needed no one on the other end at all. That is the horror of it: it still holds, without consent, without even a handler. Bring your bonds, every one; a weave that size answers to many threads pulling as one or to nothing. There is no relic this time. His bond breaking is the whole rite completed.
Then go, all of you, as one weave. He will feel every thread coming. Let him feel exactly how many.

A bond kept so long without consent that consent stopped mattering to it. He does not choose anymore; the choosing was carved out of him long ago. What you have built with yours, freely, both ways, he has the same shape of, forced. That is what you are ending.

Because his weave was built to answer a single pulling thread by consuming it, the way it consumed every wyvern fed into it. Many threads pulling together from every side, and there is finally more to cut than his weave can absorb in a breath. Alone, you are just one more thread it swallows.

The rite goes back to being spoken, not forced. I will speak it honestly again, over every bond that still wants speaking. Whether the den itself heals is not mine to promise. That the rite survives, true, is.
His weave still holds, forced and enormous. Bring every thread you have.
Still. The whole den, still, and threads I have not felt settle in longer than I can say. Tell me it is done.

Then the rite is complete, spoken true from first thread to last: freely, both directions, always. His weave could not survive being asked instead of forced, in the end. Go. Mind the thread between you. It will mind you back, for as long as you keep choosing it honestly.
Back to the thread.
I'll end the six and bring the slate.
What is this rite of binding?
What did the slate hold, once?
Why do the Young Wyverns tear at threads?
Give us time.
Here's the Force-Bonded Beast Grotto Track Slate.
Back to the thread.
I'll end the five and bring the charm.
What did the charm hold, in the old rite?
Why does a forced bond always turn?
What did the handlers do to them?
The thread needs settling first.
Here's the Force-Bonded Beast Resonant Fang Charm.
Back to the thread.
We'll bring our own bonds and cut his weave apart.
What is his bond, now?
What did the totem mark, in the old rite?
Why does one thread fail against a weave?
Our bonds are not ready to share the work.
Here's the Force-Bonded Beast Cracked Apex Totem, whole.
Back to the thread.
We'll cut every strand of their cord together.
What was braided into their cord?
What did the den-mother's token hold?
What will you restore, once the relics are whole?
Let the cord hold a little longer. We are not ready.
Here's the Force-Bonded Beast Den-Mother's Fang Token, whole.
Back to the thread.
All our bonds, together, against his.
What has his bond become?
Why does it take all of us to break one bond?
What happens after, to the rite itself?
Not yet. Our threads need to be surer.
It's done. His weave broke.
